paragraphs.title: Holiness, honoring parents, the Sabbath, and avoiding idols

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of the passage?
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “The Lord spoke unto Moses.”

easy.question: To whom was Moses to say, “Ye shall be holy”?
easy.explanation: Moses was told to speak to “all the congregation of the children of Israel.”

easy.question: What were the people warned against in verse 4?
answers: Turning to idols and making molten gods
easy.explanation: The verse forbids turning to idols or making molten gods.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites told, “Ye shall be holy”?
answers: Because the Lord their God is holy
Because they lived in the wilderness
Because they were stronger than other nations
medium.explanation: The verse explains, “I the Lord your God am holy.”

medium.question: Which command follows the command to fear and honor parents?
medium.explanation: The verse next says, “Keep my sabbaths.”

medium.question: In the phrase “molten gods,” what does “molten” mean?
answers: An idol made by casting metal
medium.explanation: A molten god is an image or idol made by casting metal.

challenge.question: What is the purpose of repeating, “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: To emphasize the Lord’s authority behind the commands
To say that Moses is God
To show that the commands are only for priests
challenge.explanation: The repetition reminds Israel that these commands come from the Lord and are binding.

challenge.question: What can we infer because “Ye shall be holy” was addressed to all Israel?
answers: The call to holiness applies to the whole community
challenge.explanation: The command is explicitly addressed to the entire congregation, not merely to leaders or priests.

challenge.question: What is the difference between “Turn ye not unto idols” and “nor make to yourselves”?
answers: The first concerns the Sabbath and the second parents
The first is singular and the second plural
The first forbids turning to idols, and the second forbids making them
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids both turning toward idols and making idols.

questions.question: What is the purpose of repeating, “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: To emphasize the Lord’s authority behind the commands
To say that Moses is God
To show that the commands are only for priests
questions.explanation: The repetition reminds Israel that these commands come from the Lord and are binding.

questions.question: What can we infer because “Ye shall be holy” was addressed to all Israel?
answers: The call to holiness applies to the whole community
questions.explanation: The command is explicitly addressed to the entire congregation, not merely to leaders or priests.

questions.question: What is the difference between “Turn ye not unto idols” and “nor make to yourselves”?
answers: The first concerns the Sabbath and the second parents
The first is singular and the second plural
The first forbids turning to idols, and the second forbids making them
questions.explanation: The verse forbids both turning toward idols and making idols.

paragraphs.title: The peace offering and eating it properly

easy.question: What kind of sacrifice is described?
easy.explanation: Verse 5 specifically mentions a sacrifice of peace offerings.

easy.question: When could the peace offering be eaten?
answers: On the day it was offered and the next day
Only on the day it was offered
easy.explanation: It was to be eaten on the day of the offering and on the following day.

easy.question: What was to be done with anything remaining until the third day?
easy.explanation: The remainder was to be burned in the fire.

medium.question: What happened if the offering was eaten on the third day?
answers: It could be eaten without restriction
medium.explanation: The text says it was abominable and would not be accepted.

medium.question: In “offer it at your own will,” what does “at your own will” mean?
medium.explanation: The offering was to be made willingly, in a manner acceptable to the Lord.

medium.question: What is the proper order for handling the offering?
answers: Burn it immediately, then eat it
Eat it only on the third day
Eat it on the first or second day, and burn the remainder
medium.explanation: It was eaten on the day of offering or the next day; the remainder was burned.

challenge.question: What is the connection between eating the offering on the third day and the punishment in verse 8?
answers: It profanes the holy thing of the Lord, so the eater bears his iniquity
It makes the person a priest
It cancels only the duty to burn it
challenge.explanation: Eating it at the forbidden time profanes what is holy, and the eater bears the guilt.

challenge.question: What is the difference between food remaining until the third day and food eaten on the third day?
answers: The remainder is burned, but eating it on the third day makes it unacceptable
The remainder may be eaten, but it is forbidden on the second day
challenge.explanation: The remainder must be burned, while eating it on the third day is explicitly condemned.

challenge.question: Why was the remainder burned instead of saved for later?
answers: To use the meat for ordinary purposes
To prevent eating it after the acceptable time
challenge.explanation: Burning it prevented continued eating after the permitted period.

questions.question: What is the connection between eating the offering on the third day and the punishment in verse 8?
answers: It profanes the holy thing of the Lord, so the eater bears his iniquity
It makes the person a priest
It cancels only the duty to burn it
questions.explanation: Eating it at the forbidden time profanes what is holy, and the eater bears the guilt.

questions.question: What is the difference between food remaining until the third day and food eaten on the third day?
answers: The remainder is burned, but eating it on the third day makes it unacceptable
The remainder may be eaten, but it is forbidden on the second day
questions.explanation: The remainder must be burned, while eating it on the third day is explicitly condemned.

questions.question: Why was the remainder burned instead of saved for later?
answers: To use the meat for ordinary purposes
To prevent eating it after the acceptable time
questions.explanation: Burning it prevented continued eating after the permitted period.

paragraphs.title: Leaving gleanings for the poor and strangers

easy.question: What part of the field was not to be harvested completely?
easy.explanation: The corners were to be left unharvested.

easy.question: For whom was the remaining produce to be left?
easy.explanation: The verse says to leave it for the poor and the stranger.

easy.question: What was not to be gathered from the vineyard?
answers: Every grape and the fallen grapes
easy.explanation: The entire vineyard was not to be gleaned.

medium.question: Why was some grain and fruit left in the field and vineyard?
answers: So the poor and stranger could take it
So the crop would immediately grow again
So it could be saved for a feast
medium.explanation: The purpose was to provide for the poor and the stranger.

medium.question: What are “gleanings” in the context of the harvest?
answers: Grain or produce left behind during harvesting
The highest part of the field
medium.explanation: Gleanings are produce missed or dropped during the harvest.

medium.question: What rule applies both to grain and grapes?
answers: They must be harvested only at night
All of them belong to the landowner
Not all the produce may be gathered; some must be left for the poor and stranger
medium.explanation: Both fields and vineyards must leave produce for others.

challenge.question: What is the difference between the corners of the field and the gleanings?
answers: The corners are deliberately left unharvested, while gleanings fall or remain during harvesting
The corners are a kind of grape, and gleanings are a kind of vineyard
challenge.explanation: The corners are left intentionally; gleanings are produce left behind during harvest.

challenge.question: In “thou shalt leave them,” what does “them” refer to?
answers: The produce left in the field and vineyard
challenge.explanation: It refers to the remaining grain and grapes left for the poor and stranger.

challenge.question: What social principle can be inferred from these commands?
answers: Only those who work the field may enjoy its produce
All produce must be gathered and divided equally
Owners have a responsibility to leave part of their property for those in need
challenge.explanation: The owner must leave part of the harvest available to the needy.

questions.question: What is the difference between the corners of the field and the gleanings?
answers: The corners are deliberately left unharvested, while gleanings fall or remain during harvesting
The corners are a kind of grape, and gleanings are a kind of vineyard
questions.explanation: The corners are left intentionally; gleanings are produce left behind during harvest.

questions.question: In “thou shalt leave them,” what does “them” refer to?
answers: The produce left in the field and vineyard
questions.explanation: It refers to the remaining grain and grapes left for the poor and stranger.

questions.question: What social principle can be inferred from these commands?
answers: Only those who work the field may enjoy its produce
All produce must be gathered and divided equally
Owners have a responsibility to leave part of their property for those in need
questions.explanation: The owner must leave part of the harvest available to the needy.

easy.question: What was forbidden in verse 11?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall not steal.”

easy.question: What was forbidden in the Lord’s name?
easy.explanation: The verse forbids swearing falsely by the Lord’s name.

easy.question: Which pair of prohibitions appears in verse 14?
answers: Cursing the deaf and tripping the blind
easy.explanation: The verse forbids cursing the deaf and putting a stumblingblock before the blind.

medium.question: What was not to happen to a hired worker’s wages?
answers: They were not to be reduced
They were not to remain overnight until morning
They were not to be paid in advance
medium.explanation: The wages were not to remain with the employer overnight.

medium.question: In “until the morning,” what does “abide with thee all night” mean?
medium.explanation: The wages were not to be withheld until the next morning.

medium.question: What is the result of swearing falsely by the Lord’s name?
medium.explanation: False oaths profane the name of God.

challenge.question: Why does the Torah forbid cursing the deaf and tripping the blind?
answers: To prevent harm to people who cannot hear the curse or see the obstacle
Because only deaf and blind people must obey the commandments
To teach that no one may speak
challenge.explanation: The commands forbid exploiting another person’s vulnerability.

challenge.question: What principle connects false swearing with the prohibitions in verse 11?
answers: Both forbid abusing speech and trust
challenge.explanation: Stealing, lying, and false swearing all damage trust and truth.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes verses 11–14?
answers: Wages, stealing, deaf and blind, swearing
Deaf and blind, swearing, wages, stealing
Stealing and lying, false swearing, fraud and wages, deaf and blind
challenge.explanation: The verses proceed in that order.

questions.question: Why does the Torah forbid cursing the deaf and tripping the blind?
answers: To prevent harm to people who cannot hear the curse or see the obstacle
Because only deaf and blind people must obey the commandments
To teach that no one may speak
questions.explanation: The commands forbid exploiting another person’s vulnerability.

questions.question: What principle connects false swearing with the prohibitions in verse 11?
answers: Both forbid abusing speech and trust
questions.explanation: Stealing, lying, and false swearing all damage trust and truth.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes verses 11–14?
answers: Wages, stealing, deaf and blind, swearing
Deaf and blind, swearing, wages, stealing
Stealing and lying, false swearing, fraud and wages, deaf and blind
questions.explanation: The verses proceed in that order.

paragraphs.title: Just judgment and responsibility toward others

easy.question: What was forbidden in judgment?
easy.explanation: The verse says not to do unrighteousness in judgment.

easy.question: How was one to treat one’s neighbor?
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

easy.question: What was forbidden along with revenge?
easy.explanation: The verse forbids both avenging and bearing a grudge.

medium.question: Why was it wrong to favor either the poor or the mighty in judgment?
answers: Because judgment must be righteous and impartial
Because only the rich are accountable
medium.explanation: The command requires righteous judgment without favoritism.

medium.question: What does “talebearer” mean in “Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer”?
medium.explanation: A talebearer spreads harmful reports about others.

medium.question: What should one do instead of hating a person in one’s heart?
medium.explanation: The verse commands one to rebuke one’s neighbor rather than harbor hatred.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour”?
answers: It is acceptable to ignore another’s danger
One must not stand by while another is in danger
challenge.explanation: The command teaches responsibility to help a neighbor in danger.

challenge.question: What is the implied difference between avenging and bearing a grudge?
answers: Avenging is an act of retaliation, while bearing a grudge is holding resentment
Avenging is love, while bearing a grudge is justice
challenge.explanation: Revenge is an outward act; a grudge is resentment retained in the heart.

challenge.question: What do “brother,” “neighbor,” and “one’s people” have in common here?
answers: They refer only to immediate family
They emphasize responsibility and love within the community
They refer only to wealthy people
challenge.explanation: These terms extend moral responsibility to the people around us.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour”?
answers: It is acceptable to ignore another’s danger
One must not stand by while another is in danger
questions.explanation: The command teaches responsibility to help a neighbor in danger.

questions.question: What is the implied difference between avenging and bearing a grudge?
answers: Avenging is an act of retaliation, while bearing a grudge is holding resentment
Avenging is love, while bearing a grudge is justice
questions.explanation: Revenge is an outward act; a grudge is resentment retained in the heart.

questions.question: What do “brother,” “neighbor,” and “one’s people” have in common here?
answers: They refer only to immediate family
They emphasize responsibility and love within the community
They refer only to wealthy people
questions.explanation: These terms extend moral responsibility to the people around us.

easy.question: What was forbidden concerning cattle?
answers: Breeding them with a diverse kind
easy.explanation: The verse forbids breeding cattle with a diverse kind.

easy.question: What was forbidden in the field?
easy.explanation: The verse forbids sowing the field with mingled seed.

easy.question: What garment was forbidden?
answers: A garment mingled of linen and wool
easy.explanation: The verse forbids a garment made of mixed linen and wool.

medium.question: In which three areas does the verse prohibit mixing kinds?
medium.explanation: The verse addresses animals, seeds, and garments.

medium.question: What does “mingled” mean in “a garment mingled of linen and wool”?
answers: Made from a prohibited mixture of materials
medium.explanation: It describes a garment made from the forbidden combination of linen and wool.

medium.question: What do the three prohibitions have in common?
medium.explanation: Each prohibition concerns mixing animals, seeds, or materials.

challenge.question: Why can “mingled” be understood as referring to mixing?
answers: It appears in contexts involving cattle, fields, and garments
It appears only beside the word garment
It names a kind of place
challenge.explanation: The same idea appears in three different contexts involving combinations.

challenge.question: What wording is distinctive in the prohibition concerning clothing?
answers: It must not come upon you
challenge.explanation: Only the garment is described as not coming upon a person.

challenge.question: What is the order of the prohibitions in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse moves from cattle, to the field, and finally to clothing.

questions.question: Why can “mingled” be understood as referring to mixing?
answers: It appears in contexts involving cattle, fields, and garments
It appears only beside the word garment
It names a kind of place
questions.explanation: The same idea appears in three different contexts involving combinations.

questions.question: What wording is distinctive in the prohibition concerning clothing?
answers: It must not come upon you
questions.explanation: Only the garment is described as not coming upon a person.

questions.question: What is the order of the prohibitions in the verse?
questions.explanation: The verse moves from cattle, to the field, and finally to clothing.

easy.question: What did the man bring to the Lord?
answers: A ram for a trespass offering
A lamb for a sin offering
easy.explanation: The man brought a ram as a trespass offering.

easy.question: Where did he bring the offering?
answers: To the door of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The offering was brought to the door of the tabernacle.

easy.question: What happened after the priest made atonement?
easy.explanation: The passage concludes that the man was forgiven.

medium.question: How is the woman described?
answers: A bondmaid betrothed to a man and not yet free
A widowed woman who was not betrothed
medium.explanation: She was a bondmaid betrothed to a man, without redemption or freedom.

medium.question: In “a bondmaid, betrothed to an husband,” what does “betrothed” mean?
answers: Promised or engaged to the man
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a woman promised or engaged to the man.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence in verses 21–22?
answers: He is forgiven, brings the ram, and the priest makes atonement
The priest makes atonement, he brings the ram, and then he sins
He brings the ram, the priest makes atonement, and then he is forgiven
medium.explanation: The offering comes first, followed by atonement and forgiveness.

challenge.question: Why were the man and woman not put to death?
answers: Because the bondmaid was not free
Because the man was a priest
challenge.explanation: The passage says they were not put to death because she was not free.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “the sin which he hath done” emphasize?
answers: That he certainly sinned many times
That atonement and forgiveness concern the specific sin committed
That the priest was the sinner
challenge.explanation: The repetition connects atonement and forgiveness with the particular offense.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the connection between the ram and forgiveness?
answers: The ram made the priest unnecessary
The ram was offered, atonement was made, and forgiveness followed
challenge.explanation: The passage presents offering, atonement, and then forgiveness.

questions.question: Why were the man and woman not put to death?
answers: Because the bondmaid was not free
Because the man was a priest
questions.explanation: The passage says they were not put to death because she was not free.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “the sin which he hath done” emphasize?
answers: That he certainly sinned many times
That atonement and forgiveness concern the specific sin committed
That the priest was the sinner
questions.explanation: The repetition connects atonement and forgiveness with the particular offense.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the connection between the ram and forgiveness?
answers: The ram made the priest unnecessary
The ram was offered, atonement was made, and forgiveness followed
questions.explanation: The passage presents offering, atonement, and then forgiveness.

paragraphs.title: The holiness of fruit over the years

easy.question: What were the Israelites to do when they entered the land?
easy.explanation: The passage says they would plant all kinds of trees for food.

easy.question: What was done with the fruit during the first three years?
answers: It was dedicated to the Lord
easy.explanation: For three years the fruit was treated as uncircumcised and not eaten.

easy.question: What was special about the fruit in the fourth year?
answers: It was holy to the Lord
easy.explanation: In the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord.

medium.question: What was the proper order for the fruit?
answers: Three years not eaten, the fourth year holy, and the fifth year eaten
Eaten in the first year and dedicated in the second
Not eaten for four years, then eaten in the sixth
medium.explanation: The fruit was not eaten for three years, was holy in the fourth, and was eaten in the fifth.

medium.question: In “three years shall it be as uncircumcised,” what does “uncircumcised” mean here?
answers: Fruit not yet permitted for eating
Fruit that had fallen from the tree
medium.explanation: The context explains that the fruit could not yet be eaten.

medium.question: Why was the fruit eaten only in the fifth year?
answers: Because the tree had no fruit earlier
Because the fourth-year fruit was sold
So that its yield might increase after the consecration
medium.explanation: The fifth-year eating is connected with increased yield.

challenge.question: How many years pass from planting the tree until its fruit may be eaten?
challenge.explanation: Three years are forbidden, the fourth is holy, and eating begins in the fifth year.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the fourth and fifth years?
answers: There is no fruit in the fourth year
The fourth-year fruit is holy to the Lord, while the fifth-year fruit may be eaten
The fourth-year fruit is sold, and a new tree is planted in the fifth
challenge.explanation: The fourth year is dedicated to the Lord; the fifth permits eating.

challenge.question: What does the progression from forbidden fruit to holy fruit to edible fruit teach?
answers: The timing of eating does not matter
Fruit exists only for farming work
Eating is permitted after waiting and dedicating the fruit to the Lord
challenge.explanation: The sequence teaches waiting, consecration, and then enjoyment.

questions.question: How many years pass from planting the tree until its fruit may be eaten?
questions.explanation: Three years are forbidden, the fourth is holy, and eating begins in the fifth year.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the fourth and fifth years?
answers: There is no fruit in the fourth year
The fourth-year fruit is holy to the Lord, while the fifth-year fruit may be eaten
The fourth-year fruit is sold, and a new tree is planted in the fifth
questions.explanation: The fourth year is dedicated to the Lord; the fifth permits eating.

questions.question: What does the progression from forbidden fruit to holy fruit to edible fruit teach?
answers: The timing of eating does not matter
Fruit exists only for farming work
Eating is permitted after waiting and dedicating the fruit to the Lord
questions.explanation: The sequence teaches waiting, consecration, and then enjoyment.

easy.question: What were the Israelites forbidden to eat?
easy.explanation: Verse 26 says not to eat anything with the blood.

easy.question: What was forbidden concerning the corners of the head?
easy.explanation: The verse forbids rounding the corners of the head.

easy.question: What mark was forbidden on the body?
easy.explanation: The verse forbids printing marks upon the body.

medium.question: Which pair of prohibitions appears in verse 26?
medium.explanation: The verse forbids eating with the blood, enchantment, and observing times.

medium.question: What does “observe times” mean in this context?
answers: Try to predict the future by signs or times
medium.explanation: It refers to divination or attempting to determine the future through signs.

medium.question: What do the prohibitions in verses 27–28 have in common?
answers: They forbid certain alterations or marks on the body
medium.explanation: They address hair, beards, cuts in the flesh, and marks on the body.

challenge.question: What does “print any marks upon you” refer to?
answers: Both cuttings in the flesh and tattoos
challenge.explanation: The phrase follows both prohibitions concerning bodily marks.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between verse 26 and verses 27–28?
answers: Verse 26 concerns eating and divination, while verses 27–28 mainly concern the body
Verse 26 is a story, while verses 27–28 are a prayer
challenge.explanation: Verse 26 addresses blood and divination; the following verses address hair and bodily marks.

challenge.question: What does the closing “I am the Lord” emphasize?
answers: The commands are merely medical advice
The commands apply only to priests
The Lord is the source of the commands and they are binding
challenge.explanation: The closing identifies the Lord as the authority behind the prohibitions.

questions.question: What does “print any marks upon you” refer to?
answers: Both cuttings in the flesh and tattoos
questions.explanation: The phrase follows both prohibitions concerning bodily marks.

questions.question: What is the main difference between verse 26 and verses 27–28?
answers: Verse 26 concerns eating and divination, while verses 27–28 mainly concern the body
Verse 26 is a story, while verses 27–28 are a prayer
questions.explanation: Verse 26 addresses blood and divination; the following verses address hair and bodily marks.

answers: The commands are merely medical advice

The Lord is the source of the commands and they are binding
questions.explanation: The closing identifies the Lord as the authority behind the prohibitions.

paragraphs.title: Family holiness, the Sabbath, and the sanctuary

easy.question: What was forbidden concerning one’s daughter?
easy.explanation: The verse forbids prostituting one’s daughter.

easy.question: What could happen if a daughter was prostituted?
answers: The land would become full of wickedness
easy.explanation: The verse warns that the land could become full of wickedness.

easy.question: What did verse 30 command the people to keep?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall keep my sabbaths.”

medium.question: What is the connection between prostituting a daughter and the land?
answers: The act could cause the land to become full of wickedness
The act would enlarge the land
medium.explanation: The verse connects the personal sin with corruption throughout the land.

medium.question: What does “prostitute” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: The context describes a serious violation of the daughter’s dignity and holiness.

medium.question: What is the order of ideas in these verses?
answers: Reverence for the sanctuary, Sabbath observance, then prostitution
Sabbath observance, prostitution, then the land’s wickedness
Prohibition of prostitution, its result, then the Sabbath and sanctuary
medium.explanation: Verse 29 gives the prohibition and consequence; verse 30 addresses the Sabbath and sanctuary.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from linking prostitution with the land becoming full of wickedness?
answers: Personal behavior can affect the wider society and land
Only leaders are responsible for such actions
The land itself can prostitute people
challenge.explanation: The verse presents a personal act as having communal consequences.

challenge.question: Why does verse 30 end with “I am the Lord”?
answers: To identify the location of the sanctuary
To emphasize the Lord’s authority behind the commands
challenge.explanation: The closing grounds the commands in the Lord’s authority.

challenge.question: What common idea appears in verses 29–30?
answers: Maintaining holiness in human relationships and worship
challenge.explanation: The verses address sexual holiness, the Sabbath, and reverence for the sanctuary.

questions.question: What can be inferred from linking prostitution with the land becoming full of wickedness?
answers: Personal behavior can affect the wider society and land
Only leaders are responsible for such actions
The land itself can prostitute people
questions.explanation: The verse presents a personal act as having communal consequences.

questions.question: Why does verse 30 end with “I am the Lord”?
answers: To identify the location of the sanctuary
To emphasize the Lord’s authority behind the commands
questions.explanation: The closing grounds the commands in the Lord’s authority.

questions.question: What common idea appears in verses 29–30?
answers: Maintaining holiness in human relationships and worship
questions.explanation: The verses address sexual holiness, the Sabbath, and reverence for the sanctuary.

paragraphs.title: The prohibition against familiar spirits and wizards

easy.question: To whom were the Israelites forbidden to turn?
answers: Those with familiar spirits and wizards
easy.explanation: The verse forbids turning to those with familiar spirits and to wizards.

easy.question: What were the Israelites forbidden to seek?
easy.explanation: They were not to seek to be defiled through such practices.

easy.question: Who gives the command in the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse ends, “I am the Lord your God.”

medium.question: What is the connection between consulting them and defilement?
answers: Consulting them is a way of becoming defiled
Consulting them has no connection with defilement
medium.explanation: The verse links seeking them with becoming defiled.

medium.question: What are “familiar spirits” in this context?
answers: People who claim to communicate with spirits or the dead
medium.explanation: The context places them beside wizards and forbidden spiritual practices.

medium.question: What additional action is forbidden besides turning to them?
answers: Seeking to be defiled through them
medium.explanation: The verse forbids both consulting them and seeking defilement through them.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated command “regard not” and “neither seek”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to wizards
challenge.explanation: The two commands emphasize both avoiding consultation and avoiding pursuit of such practices.

challenge.question: Why does the verse end, “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: To emphasize that the command comes from the Lord’s authority
To explain who the wizards are
challenge.explanation: The ending identifies the Lord as the source of the prohibition.

challenge.question: What does “by them” refer to in “to be defiled by them”?
answers: Those with familiar spirits and wizards
challenge.explanation: It refers back to the familiar spirits and wizards.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repeated command “regard not” and “neither seek”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to wizards
questions.explanation: The two commands emphasize both avoiding consultation and avoiding pursuit of such practices.

questions.question: Why does the verse end, “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: To emphasize that the command comes from the Lord’s authority
To explain who the wizards are
questions.explanation: The ending identifies the Lord as the source of the prohibition.

questions.question: What does “by them” refer to in “to be defiled by them”?
answers: Those with familiar spirits and wizards
questions.explanation: It refers back to the familiar spirits and wizards.

easy.question: What was one to do before a hoary head?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head.”

easy.question: How should one treat an old man?
easy.explanation: The verse commands people to honor the face of the old man.

easy.question: Who says, “I am the Lord”?
easy.explanation: The closing words identify the Lord as the speaker.

medium.question: What is the connection between honoring the elderly and fearing God?
answers: Respecting the elderly is part of obeying God
medium.explanation: The verse connects respect for the elderly with reverence for God.

medium.question: What does “rise up” mean in this verse?
medium.explanation: It means to stand in respect before an older person.

medium.question: What is the order of the commands?
answers: Fear God, rise, and honor the elderly
Honor the elderly, fear God, and rise
